items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Jimmie Davis who was known as Jimmie "Lover Man" Davis because he was one of the co-composers of the famous song, "Lover Man" was engaged as an entertainer.

ctx.x: In Nice, I worked with Bernard Peiffer, Huber Fol who had been in the Clarke-Lobo orchestra. Hubert told me that the later orchestra didn't last long because Frisco wanted the French musicians to continue to play when the Americans would take a rest and the place was not going to well as far as business was concerned. Kenny and Lobo did not agree with the way Frisco wanted the band to play and that didn't help either the situation, so the band broke up after a few weeks.

The other musicians in the Nice deal were Jack Smaley on bass, and a young white American drummer named Richie Frost. Jimmie Davis who was known as Jimmie "Lover Man" Davis because he was one of the co-composers of the famous song, "Lover Man" was engaged as an entertainer. Another singer engaged there was Monique Davis who was French
